reason: The developing red cells contain growing protein chains, and haemoglobin's building materials look like a useful starting pair for oxygen-carrying blood.
expectation: The developing cells will use the materials to make haemoglobin.

effect: The materials made mature red blood cells with haemoglobin; plasma still needs assembling.
reaction: It was interesting that the mature cells no longer have nuclei.
reason: Plasma water and solutes look like the fluid components needed for the blood sample.
expectation: The solutes will dissolve in the water to make plasma.

effect: Plasma is ready, so I can add the red blood cells to the fluid.
reaction: The yellow plasma was a little surprising.
reason: Red blood cells and plasma are both components of the blood sample.
expectation: The red blood cells will be suspended in the plasma.

effect: The cells had to bind oxygen before joining the sample; the result also shows haemoglobin can release oxygen where it is low.
reaction: I was surprised that adding the cells to plasma was not available first.
reason: The oxygen-bearing red cells and plasma are components of the intended blood sample, so I will try them together now.
expectation: The oxygen-bearing cells will be suspended in plasma.

effect: The oxygen-bearing red cells are now suspended in plasma; the sample still lacks white cells and platelets.
reaction: The picture makes the remaining missing components clear.
reason: White cells and platelets are the remaining blood components shown on the board.
expectation: They will join the red cells in plasma to complete the blood sample.

effect: Adding white cells and platelets completed the blood sample and showed its different components together.
reaction: Seeing the completed sample made the separate parts easier to picture.

mostWorthwhile.text: The oxygen step was most worthwhile: it showed that haemoglobin can both bind and release oxygen, especially where dissolved oxygen is low.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making plasma was straightforward but less informative than seeing how the red cells carry oxygen.

surprise.text: I was surprised that mature red blood cells lack nuclei, and that the game would not let me add them to plasma before they carried oxygen.

arbitrary.text: Requiring oxygen to be added before the red cells could join plasma felt like a game prerequisite; the explanation did not make clear why that order was necessary.

continue.text: I might continue for another chapter to see how circulation brings oxygen carriers close to cells, though this chapter's assembly was mostly predictable.
